item.itunes:title: 嚴重災情 iPhone Duo 怎麼辦？
item.itunes:author: 蘋果爹

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fffx1-FNbzI

值得閱讀的理由

  • 整理網路上折疊螢幕裂痕的案例，區分重複轉載與較可信的第一手回報。
  • 透過鉸鏈結構與 iFixit 的拆解推測，說明螢幕可能在何處、為何受損。
  • 分析問題可能來自組裝瑕疵或量產環節，也提醒讀者留意折疊機構的脆弱處。
  • 提供已購買產品的用戶處理方向，並分享作者實際使用與測試後的觀察。

摘要

網路裂痕案例：數量有限，破損位置卻高度相似

新款 iPhone 開賣不到一週，網路上便出現多起內螢幕裂開的照片與影片。彭回顧先前曾提醒消費者，初代產品需要經過大量用戶實測，才能看出耐用度與量產問題；這次他們也整理不同社群和論壇的資訊，希望釐清狀況。剔除重複貼文與造假的照片後，目前約有50 起通報，其中包括來自 11 個國家和地區的第一手回報及用戶照片。彭也指出，實際案例可能多於公開數字，因為有人會直接換機，未必在網路上發文。

共同特徵：多在短時間內沿同一位置裂開

較可信的案例呈現出相似情況：用戶開闔手機時感到卡住，勉強施力後聽見「喀」的一聲，螢幕便沿著折線出現一道長裂痕，附近還可能延伸出另一道裂紋。許多案例在拿到手機不到 24 小時、折疊不到 20 次時就發生，有些甚至在店內設定手機時便出現；有無裝保護殼似乎也不影響。這些共同點使彭認為，問題較不像長期使用或摔落造成，而可能與特定批次的組裝瑕疵有關。

鉸鏈結構與可能的裂痕成因

彭接著說明，鉸鏈包含一百多個零件；手機展開時，兩片碳纖維板與中央支撐條共同支撐螢幕。摺疊時，螢幕會在鉸鏈內形成水滴狀彎曲，而中央支撐條必須先向下退開，留出彎折空間。根據 iFixit 拆解、CT 掃描與模型模擬提出的推測，如果支撐條沒有完全下降，螢幕彎曲處便可能碰撞支撐條，讓力量集中在一點，最後導致破裂。彭指出，公開照片裡的裂痕大多位於鉸鏈中下方、排線通道下方，也就是支撐條起始的位置；雖然目前仍屬推論，但位置的一致性讓他認為這個解釋相當可能。

彭的判斷：可定位是好消息，脆弱結構仍值得注意

彭認同 iFixit 的推測，並認為多起故障都出現在相同位置，從排查角度來看反而是相對好的消息，因為問題更容易被定位與修正。不過，他也提醒，鉸鏈與折疊螢幕本身存在較脆弱的區域，灰塵或細砂若卡在附近，可能妨礙機構完全摺合，增加受損風險。彭推測，蘋果或許正在追查量產流程或零件批次；若只是小範圍組裝失誤，後續批次可能很快改善，若涉及難以避免的良率問題，則可能需要從設計層面處理。

作者實測與已購用戶的處理方式

彭表示，手上的手機使用近六天，已開闔超過百次，也經過測試、跑分與遊戲等使用情境，目前尚未發現螢幕異常；不過，看到大量裂痕消息後，他折疊手機時變得格外小心，也會留意是否出現異音，認為這多少影響了使用體驗。對於已經購買手機的人，影片提到蘋果在 10 月 26 日表示已注意到少數螢幕問題，若遇到狀況可聯絡 AppleCare 詢問換機；不一定要購買 AppleCare+，但需由蘋果確認屬於製造問題。透過電信業者購買的用戶，也可循此方式聯絡處理。

================================================

People have been asking why we haven't talked about the incidents, so today we're going to talk about them. The iPhone went on sale five days ago, and photos of the inner screen cracking have been circulating online everywhere . It's not just a typical crease; the screen is actually splitting. They say that when opening it, you first hear a "click," and when you unfold it further , there's another "crack." Then, you'll see a split right in the middle, following where the screen should fold, and simultaneously, another white crack appears in the same area. If you look closely, they are all breaking in the exact same spot. But what if I told you that if so many units are breaking in the exact same place, it might actually be good news? Do you think that's. possible? Let's begin. Hey everyone, I'm Peng. Back in September, when we made our "Think Twice Before Buying" video, I said you don't need to spend 75,000 to be a guinea pig; we'll buy it instead. So, when it went on sale on October 23rd, in less than a week, there were already over 50 reported incidents online, and they are all breaking in the same spot. Of course, we've collected all this information to help provide some analysis for everyone . In our previous video, we also mentioned that for first-generation products, to truly evaluate their durability or the issues encountered in mass production, you have to wait until they are in the hands of real users and tested in large batches to see the. truth. Although we expected this, seeing how serious the phenomenon is still makes us a bit worried. We believe that by researching this problem thoroughly, maybe we can put everyone's mind at ease a little bit? So, I will divide this video into three parts. The first is discussing the cases reported online—which ones are legitimate. Second, some people have taken the hinge apart to study what exactly is going wrong, and we will share our own views. Third, if you have already bought one and are seeing this now, what should you do? Before we start, if you like this type of video, please remember to hit the like button, leave a comment below to share your thoughts, or subscribe to the channel. Alright, first point: let's start by addressing the screen issues everyone.

is talking about. It actually looks like a lot, but after researching Reddit, Xiaohongshu, Douyin, TikTok, and forums like MR, some of these reports are actually duplicate cases. If we keep looking, after filtering out the many reposts, there are only about 50 cases so far. Of course, we know this number doesn't represent everyone who encountered it, as many might just go to the manufacturer for a replacement. First, Apple hasn't really disclosed how many cases there are, claiming it's a minority. Second, you can't see the many people who didn't post or those who noticed it right when unboxing and just swapped it out. So,. the more news and discussion there is, the higher the buzz; like the "Bendgate " with the iPhone 6 Plus back in the day, I heard only nine people reported it, but it was spread around and felt like a very serious issue. At the same time, we've seen that many photos are fake. In one, you can see the calendar says Thursday the 23rd, but the 23rd was clearly a Friday, and the author admitted to using GPT to alter the photo. As of now, we’ve counted reports from 11 countries and regions, including 27 photos posted by the users themselves and first-hand reports. I think this second set of numbers is more important, as we can see the. commonalities in how they broke. As we just mentioned, many people feel it get stuck when opening, and when they force it, they hear a "click" sound. The cracks look very similar. Some heard this sound when folding it. The point is always the same: a long crack along the vertical line—not a crease—and then a crack extending across at the same point. Most of this happens within 24 hours of getting it, with maybe fewer than 20 folds. Some people had it crack right in the store while setting it up, and it happened to both those with and without cases. So, these common points make it look less like it was from long-term use or being dropped.

; it’s likely that there was a flaw during assembly for that specific batch . In the next part, we'll look at the hinge to see where the problem lies and why it cracks. We need to look at its internal structure first, and there are over 100 parts in the hinge mechanism. So when the screen is unfolded, there are two carbon fiber plates underneath, one on the left and one on the right, with a support strip in the middle. The three work together to keep the screen flat. But when you fold it, the screen doesn't just form a straight line; it actually bends inside the hinge into a teardrop shape. At the widest part of that teardrop fold, they say it's about 3.85 millimeters. To bend into this. teardrop shape, the center support strip must first retract downward to make room for the teardrop curve below. iFixit took it apart, used CT scanning, and built a model to simulate the folding process. Their theory is that if the support strip doesn't descend all the way, the screen's teardrop curve will hit the support strip and be pressed against it while folding. In this situation, when all the force is concentrated on one point and you force it to bend, it might crack. If you stack up all the photos shared by users , the location of the cracks is actually the same place: right in the. middle-lower part of the hinge, directly below the gap where the ribbon cable passes through, which is where the support strip begins. Although this can only be called a theory for now, given how similar the locations look in all the photos people have shared, I think it's almost certainly the issue. Next part, let's talk about my judg-- ment. I actually agree with iFixit's assessment regarding the aforementioned problem, because when we usually look for where a problem originates, the first thing we check is whether the issue can be replicated. If so many people are experiencing the same failure at the same point, I would consider that relatively good news. This isn't to take Apple's side, but.

from the perspective of troubleshooting , it means the problem can be isolated, which saves a lot of time if you want to resolve it. But at the same time, the bad news is that while this batch of phones might just be poorly assembled, it's unavoidable that it inherently has a very fragile point. Apple markets it as water-resistant, but the hinge end is actually very prone to dust ingress. While we can't say that fine sand getting inside will definitely cause the same issue, the problem point we're seeing now is right at the water-drop hinge of the folding screen and the support plate beneath it . If a grain of sand happens to get stuck nearby—even if it doesn't get. inside—it could obstruct the adjacent structure and prevent a complete fold, which might lead to this situation. We might think that since folding phones have been out for so many years, this should be a basic issue. My assessment is that Apple likely doesn't have a major problem with the design itself, because they surely have many test units on hand, and they shouldn't have encountered this after their extensive internal testing. But we know that once any product enters mass production, you can't just assume the most perfect scenario. Once you move to factory mass production, with so many people handling it across different facilities , even a small issue in a precise. component can impact the entire structure—especially if it hits that fragile, flexible screen. When there are too many variables, these kinds of problems occur more frequently and are easily amplified. These same small issues might not happen in a standard, non-folding phone like an iPhone 15 Pro , simply because there is no folding mechanism to worry about. Therefore, I think they are already looking into the mass production chain to see which step or which batch of parts went wrong. If it’s a simple error, it’s easy to handle. But if it’s a yield-rate issue that's hard to avoid in mass production, it’s very likely they’ll have to resolve it at the fundamental design level. Minor.

adjustments to small parts might be implemented in the next batch quickly, but if a large-scale design overhaul is needed, that might have to wait for the next generation. Regardless, we must say that this type of issue shouldn't happen, but at least for now, it seems to be limited to a small batch and should be solvable. Right, many people might ask, how many times have we opened it so far? I feel like it's definitely been over a hundred times. We've been using this unit for nearly six days, which isn't a short time. It's been handled by many people, and I've performed extensive testing, benchmarks, and even played Arena of Valor on it. When you're playing and get excited, you're bound to put some. pressure on it. Many people say you can touch the crease in the middle to see if there's a bump, but honestly, I don't really feel anything obvious when I touch it. As of the time of writing, we haven't encountered any screen issues, but we will continue to monitor it. It would be a lie to say I'm not worried; after seeing so much news, I'm actually being extra careful when folding it now. Sometimes when opening or closing, I worry about hearing any strange noises, because if I did, I would stop immediately. So, I do feel this has affected the user experience a little bit. Okay, for the next part, what should you do if you have already bought one? Actually, Apple issued a statement on October 26th saying they. are aware that a very small number of iPhones might have screen issues, and if you have problems, you can contact AppleCare to exchange it; you don't actually need to have AppleCare +. As long as they can confirm it's a manufacturing issue, they will help you replace it. It's the same if you bought it through a carrier; you can contact AppleCare, but the premise is that they must have stock. In the cases we compiled, 11 units were replaced on the spot, while 8 units were approved for replacement after inspection, but they were out of stock, especially the 1TB and 2TB models. In the U.S., if you need to mail it in for repair, they might send you a new one first, and once you receive it, you send the old one back, but there will be a $ 2,500.

USD deposit. Also, there are five cases where they claimed it was human error —that it was dropped—and that the customer had to pay, but these five happened before Apple's statement, so we don't know how they are handled now, or if those five were truly dropped by the users. I think many people worry about the claim of human error because the hinge isn't serviced separately; if the hinge breaks and affects the screen , the official repair method is to replace the entire display assembly or give you a brand-new unit. Without a warranty, that costs $ 999 USD in the U.S., and over 30,000 NTD in Taiwan. So if you have already bought one, I think. there are a few things you can do. First, open and check the device immediately. You might want someone to record it for you, confirming that you don't encounter any issues while opening, closing, and folding the device, as we know many cases happen exactly when opening or closing it. Second, if you feel any resistance or issues when opening or closing, don't force it; contact the store immediately to handle the problem. Third, if it does crack, you can use Apple's statement from October 26th and take it to an Apple Store to discuss it. In this case, you wouldn't even need AppleCare +. Fourth, if you are still within the return period, consider. whether you are worried about this issue. Maybe you want to wait until they confirm what the problem is and release a batch without issues before buying it; I think that is also an option. For those who haven't bought one yet, I suggest the same as before. Unless you really need it, I don't think you have to buy the first-generation product given the current level of maturity. Plus, the durability tests currently have too few samples and not enough time. This minor issue might just be the beginning, and it's hard to say what other problems might arise with long-term use. Right now, the product is in a stage where its applications and optimizations.

aren't fully mature, so I don't think there's a need to spend extra money and invite trouble. Returning to the question at the beginning, the fact that so many units are failing at the same spot might actually be good news for Apple, as it makes it easier to pinpoint the exact issue and suggests they can easily fix it. I am not trying to speak for Apple, because after all, I didn't recommend everyone to buy this unit, but I think these two parts should be kept separate; not recommending a purchase......does not mean I lack confidence in Apple's design and after-sales service. Based on Apple's past after-sales service and their responsible attitude, I believe that for issues that have been widely. reported as defects, they will definitely address them. However, I still maintain my previous advice: if you must buy this device, remember to factor in the cost of AppleCare +, especially if you plan to keep it for more than a year. So, of course, regardless of warranties or repairs, that doesn't cover up the fact that there might be some structural vulnerabilities. The suppliers for foldable phones have always been the same, so if anyone previously imagined that since they waited seven years to launch a foldable, they might have some "black tech" solution from these suppliers? Sorry, but after taking it apart, there really isn't one. Even if they have a clever solution for the crease on their foldable screen, once. you remove the matte layer, the crease is actually just like other foldables. So fundamentally, Apple hasn't reinvented anything; it’s still just a very expensive flexible screen. Yeah, for those who still want to buy it, or like me, have no choice but to buy it, just use it carefully and protect it well. It’s a delicate device, so just don't be too rough with it. We will continue to use this device, and my initial impression is that there are just too many compromises. I hope to see more optimizations that make it feel like a truly worthwhile product. We will share our long-term usage experience and let you all know if any issues arise. That’s it for today’s video. Don’t forget to like and subscribe. See you next time, bye!

is talking about. It actually looks like a lot, but after researching Reddit, Xiaohongshu, Douyin, TikTok, and forums like MR, some of these reports are actually duplicate cases. Most of this happens within 24 hours of getting it, with maybe fewer than 20 folds. Some people had it crack right in the store while setting it up, and it happened to both those with and without cases. ; it’s likely that there was a flaw during assembly for that specific batch . In the next part, we'll look at the hinge to see where the problem lies and why it cracks. adjustments to small parts might be implemented in the next batch quickly, but if a large-scale design overhaul is needed, that might have to wait for the next generation. USD deposit. Fourth, if you are still within the return period, consider. whether you are worried about this issue. aren't fully mature, so I don't think there's a need to spend extra money and invite trouble. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 整理網路上折疊螢幕裂痕的案例，區分重複轉載與較可信的第一手回報。
  • 透過鉸鏈結構與 iFixit 的拆解推測，說明螢幕可能在何處、為何受損。
  • 分析問題可能來自組裝瑕疵或量產環節，也提醒讀者留意折疊機構的脆弱處。
  • 提供已購買產品的用戶處理方向，並分享作者實際使用與測試後的觀察。

摘要

網路裂痕案例：數量有限，破損位置卻高度相似

新款 iPhone 開賣不到一週，網路上便出現多起內螢幕裂開的照片與影片。彭回顧先前曾提醒消費者，初代產品需要經過大量用戶實測，才能看出耐用度與量產問題；這次他們也整理不同社群和論壇的資訊，希望釐清狀況。剔除重複貼文與造假的照片後，目前約有50 起通報，其中包括來自 11 個國家和地區的第一手回報及用戶照片。彭也指出，實際案例可能多於公開數字，因為有人會直接換機，未必在網路上發文。

共同特徵：多在短時間內沿同一位置裂開

較可信的案例呈現出相似情況：用戶開闔手機時感到卡住，勉強施力後聽見「喀」的一聲，螢幕便沿著折線出現一道長裂痕，附近還可能延伸出另一道裂紋。許多案例在拿到手機不到 24 小時、折疊不到 20 次時就發生，有些甚至在店內設定手機時便出現；有無裝保護殼似乎也不影響。這些共同點使彭認為，問題較不像長期使用或摔落造成，而可能與特定批次的組裝瑕疵有關。

鉸鏈結構與可能的裂痕成因

彭接著說明，鉸鏈包含一百多個零件；手機展開時，兩片碳纖維板與中央支撐條共同支撐螢幕。摺疊時，螢幕會在鉸鏈內形成水滴狀彎曲，而中央支撐條必須先向下退開，留出彎折空間。根據 iFixit 拆解、CT 掃描與模型模擬提出的推測，如果支撐條沒有完全下降，螢幕彎曲處便可能碰撞支撐條，讓力量集中在一點，最後導致破裂。彭指出，公開照片裡的裂痕大多位於鉸鏈中下方、排線通道下方，也就是支撐條起始的位置；雖然目前仍屬推論，但位置的一致性讓他認為這個解釋相當可能。

彭的判斷：可定位是好消息，脆弱結構仍值得注意

彭認同 iFixit 的推測，並認為多起故障都出現在相同位置，從排查角度來看反而是相對好的消息，因為問題更容易被定位與修正。不過，他也提醒，鉸鏈與折疊螢幕本身存在較脆弱的區域，灰塵或細砂若卡在附近，可能妨礙機構完全摺合，增加受損風險。彭推測，蘋果或許正在追查量產流程或零件批次；若只是小範圍組裝失誤，後續批次可能很快改善，若涉及難以避免的良率問題，則可能需要從設計層面處理。

作者實測與已購用戶的處理方式

彭表示，手上的手機使用近六天，已開闔超過百次，也經過測試、跑分與遊戲等使用情境，目前尚未發現螢幕異常；不過，看到大量裂痕消息後，他折疊手機時變得格外小心，也會留意是否出現異音，認為這多少影響了使用體驗。對於已經購買手機的人，影片提到蘋果在 10 月 26 日表示已注意到少數螢幕問題，若遇到狀況可聯絡 AppleCare 詢問換機；不一定要購買 AppleCare+，但需由蘋果確認屬於製造問題。透過電信業者購買的用戶，也可循此方式聯絡處理。

aren't fully mature, so I don't think there's a need to spend extra money and invite trouble. Returning to the question at the beginning, the fact that so many units are failing at the same spot might actually be good news for Apple, as it makes it easier to pinpoint the exact issue and suggests they can easily fix it. I am not trying to speak for Apple, because after all, I didn't recommend everyone to buy this unit, but I think these two parts should be kept separate; not recommending a purchase......does not mean I lack confidence in Apple's design and after-sales service. Based on Apple's past after-sales service and their responsible attitude, I believe that for issues that have been widely. reported as defects, they will definitely address them. However, I still maintain my previous advice: if you must buy this device, remember to factor in the cost of AppleCare +, especially if you plan to keep it for more than a year. So, of course, regardless of warranties or repairs, that doesn't cover up the fact that there might be some structural vulnerabilities. The suppliers for foldable phones have always been the same, so if anyone previously imagined that since they waited seven years to launch a foldable, they might have some "black tech" solution from these suppliers? Sorry, but after taking it apart, there really isn't one. Even if they have a clever solution for the crease on their foldable screen, once. you remove the matte layer, the crease is actually just like other foldables. So fundamentally, Apple hasn't reinvented anything; it’s still just a very expensive flexible screen. Yeah, for those who still want to buy it, or like me, have no choice but to buy it, just use it carefully and protect it well. It’s a delicate device, so just don't be too rough with it. We will continue to use this device, and my initial impression is that there are just too many compromises. I hope to see more optimizations that make it feel like a truly worthwhile product. We will share our long-term usage experience and let you all know if any issues arise. That’s it for today’s video. Don’t forget to like and subscribe. See you next time, bye!

值得閱讀的理由

  • 比較 iPhone Duo 與 iPad mini 的價格、效能、螢幕及續航，幫助讀者理解兩種裝置的差異。
  • 說明摺疊手機與手機加平板的使用取捨，涵蓋耐用性、維修風險與日常便利性。
  • 整理 iPad mini 在多工、外接螢幕、手寫筆記與創作上的優勢，提供不同族群的選購參考。

摘要

裝置定位與硬體差異

作者從重量與價格切入比較 iPhone Duo 和 iPad mini。兩者重量相近，但 iPhone Duo 價格高出許多。兩款裝置皆搭載 A20 Pro 處理器，不過 iPad mini 機身較大，散熱空間更充裕；螢幕方面，iPad mini 提供較大的硬質 OLED 螢幕與奈米紋理玻璃選項，iPhone Duo 則採用可摺疊的軟性內螢幕，表面保護膜相對需要留意。

便攜、續航與多工體驗

iPhone Duo 能摺疊收納，且相機規格較強，但摺疊結構也伴隨較高的損壞風險與維修成本；若送修，還可能影響日常通訊。作者也提醒，使用摺疊手機長時間追劇或玩遊戲，會消耗原本供手機通訊使用的電量；手機和平板分開使用，則能分擔電力需求。系統方面，iPad mini 的 iPadOS 支援多視窗、外接 4K 螢幕及鍵盤操作，更適合多工與工作情境。

手寫、價格與適用族群

在手寫與繪圖方面，iPhone Duo 僅支援 Apple Pencil USB-C，功能較為基本；iPad mini 則支援 Apple Pencil Pro，可使用感壓、旋轉筆刷與磁吸收納等功能。作者指出，同容量下 iPhone Duo 比 iPad mini 貴約 48,500 元；即使搭配 iPhone Pro，與 iPad mini 組成雙裝置，總價仍可能低於單買 iPhone Duo，而且兩台設備可以各自升級汰換。偏好只帶一台設備、又需要大螢幕的人較適合考慮 iPhone Duo；常做筆記的學生與需要壓感繪圖的創作者，則更適合 iPad mini。

工作與娛樂使用建議

iPad mini 可作為 Mac 筆電的延伸螢幕，並受惠於較成熟的 iPadOS 與專業 App，適合外出工作、商務展示和多工處理。它的大螢幕也適合追劇、閱讀漫畫；對已經使用 Pro Max 等大尺寸手機的人而言，搭配 iPad mini 能增加閱讀與觀影空間。整體而言，作者認為多數人選擇現有手機搭配 iPad mini，通常比購入昂貴的摺疊手機更划算，也更能兼顧彈性與使用體驗。
